Chunking the datasets will allow the app to be run in shiny.io

```{r Custom 200km grid square shapefile}

#The 10km chunks are too small for Andrew to upload to the geoserver

#CEH land cover map 2023
lcm <- raster("C:/Users/aalg1m25/OneDrive - University of Southampton/Documents/GitHub/iDeer/data/gblcm2023_25m.tif")

#focal1000 dams raster
dams <- raster("C:/Users/ik929086/OneDrive - University of Southampton/R_data_transfer/Amy-iDeer-tool/data/focal_DAMS_1000m.tif")

res <- 200000 # change this to something which splits the country into the desired 4-5 sections.
e <- ext(lcm) #lcm = template raster

# Manually extend to ensure full coverage
x_seq <- seq(e[1], e[2] + res, by = res)
y_seq <- seq(e[3], e[4] + res, by = res)

# Create polygons
grid_polys <- list()
id <- 1

for (i in seq_along(x_seq[-length(x_seq)])) {
  for (j in seq_along(y_seq[-length(y_seq)])) {
    x1 <- x_seq[i]; x2 <- x_seq[i+1]
    y1 <- y_seq[j]; y2 <- y_seq[j+1]
    coords <- matrix(c(x1,y1, x2,y1, x2,y2, x1,y2, x1,y1), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)
    grid_polys[[id]] <- vect(list(coords), type = "polygons", crs = as.character(crs(lcm)))
    id <- id + 1
  }
}

# Combine into a single SpatVector
grid <- do.call(rbind, grid_polys)

# Optional: assign IDs
grid$id <- seq_len(nrow(grid))

#Give tiles names
grid$tile_name <- paste0("tile_", seq_len(nrow(grid)))
names(grid)

grid <- st_as_sf(grid)
st_crs(grid) <- 27700 #ignore warning, crs is correct

# Save as ESRI Shapefile (creates .shp + associated files)
st_write(grid, "C:/Users/aalg1m25/OneDrive - University of Southampton/Documents/GitHub/iDeer/output/custom_grid_200km.shp", overwrite = TRUE)

# Plot geometries
plot(grid$geometry, main = "Custom 200km Grid", col = "lightblue", border = "grey40")
plot(lcm, add=TRUE)

plot(grid$geometry, main = "Custom 200km Grid", col = "lightblue", border = "grey40")
plot(dams, add=TRUE)

##

```

```{r Raw NFI dataset chunked to 200km}
nfi <- st_read("~/iDeer/data/raw-data/nfi-2023-raw/National_Forest_Inventory_GB_2023.shp")
st_crs(nfi) <- 27700

nfi_output_dir <- "C:/Users/ik929086/Documents/iDeer/output/nfi_chunked_200km"
nfi_per_tile <- split_wood_polys_by_tile(wood_polys = nfi,
                                  tiles = grid,
                                  output_dir = nfi_output_dir)

nfi_tiled_files <-list.files(nfi_output_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
nfi_files <- lapply(nfi_tiled_files, readRDS)

# Read in RDS files
nfi_tiled_files <- list.files(nfi_output_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
nfi_files <- lapply(nfi_tiled_files, readRDS)

# Extract tile_IDs from each list of RDS files
nfi_tile_ids <- sapply(nfi_files, function(x) unique(x$tile_ID))

# Simplify geometries with a tolerance of 5 metres
nfi_files_simplified <- lapply(nfi_files, function(x) {
  st_simplify(x, dTolerance = 5, preserveTopology = TRUE)
})

#save simplified tiles
simplified_nfi_dir <- "C:/Users/ik929086/Documents/iDeer/output/nfi_chunked_200m_simplified_5m"

# Save each simplified RDS using original filenames
invisible(mapply(function(data, original_file) {
  file_name <- basename(original_file)
  saveRDS(data, file.path(simplified_nfi_dir, file_name))
}, nfi_files_simplified, nfi_tiled_files))

```

```{r Chunk-raw-nfi-into-5}

nfi <- st_read("~/iDeer/data/raw-data/nfi-2023-raw/National_Forest_Inventory_GB_2023.shp")
st_crs(nfi) <- 27700

nfi_output_dir <- "C:/Users/ik929086/Documents/iDeer/output/nfi_EW_chunked"

                                  tiles = EW_chunks,
                                  output_dir = nfi_output_dir,
                                  file_prefix = "nfi_EW_chunked_")

nfi_tiled_files <-list.files(nfi_output_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
nfi_files <- lapply(nfi_tiled_files, readRDS)

# Read in RDS files
nfi_tiled_files <- list.files(nfi_output_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
nfi_files <- lapply(nfi_tiled_files, readRDS)

# Extract tile_IDs from each list of RDS files
nfi_tile_ids <- sapply(nfi_files, function(x) unique(x$tile_ID))

# Simplify geometries with a tolerance of 5 metres
nfi_files_simplified <- lapply(nfi_files, function(x) {
  st_simplify(x, dTolerance = 5, preserveTopology = TRUE)
})

#save simplified tiles
simplified_nfi_dir <- "C:/Users/ik929086/Documents/iDeer/output/nfi_EW_chunked_simplified_5m"

#save as shapefiles for Andrew
mapply(function(data, original_file) {
  # Extract base filename without extension
  base_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(original_file))
  # Construct full path for shapefile (must end with .shp)
  shp_path <- file.path(simplified_nfi_dir, paste0(base_name, ".shp"))
  # Write shapefile, overwrite if exists
  st_write(data, shp_path, delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
}, nfi_files_simplified , nfi_tiled_files )

# List all shapefiles in the output directory
nfi_shp_files <- list.files(simplified_nfi_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE)
nfi_shp_data <- lapply(nfi_shp_files, st_read, quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r Code-for-testing-st_simplify-tolerance}

# Calculate sizes in bytes for the original files
sizes_before <- sapply(nfi_files, object.size)
# Calculate sizes in bytes for the simplified files
sizes_after  <- sapply(nfi_files_simplified, object.size)

# Create a data frame for clear comparison
comparison <- data.frame(
  tile_ID = nfi_tile_ids,
  size_before_bytes = sizes_before,
  size_after_bytes = sizes_after,
  reduction_percent = round(100 * (1 - sizes_after / sizes_before), 2)
)

# Pick a tile index to inspect
i <- 1  # you can change this index to view other tiles

# Original and simplified objects
original_geom <- nfi_files[[i]]
simplified_geom <- nfi_files_simplified[[i]]

# Create plots
p1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = original_geom, fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  ggtitle("Original Geometry") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = simplified_geom, fill = "lightgreen", color = "black") +
  ggtitle("Simplified Geometry (100m)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine plots side by side
p1
p2

#export to shapefiles to compare in ArcGIS
  st_write(nfi_files[[i]], "C:/Users/ik929086/Documents/iDeer/output/Testing/original_polys_pre_simplify_TEST.shp", delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
  st_write(nfi_files_simplified[[i]], "C:/Users/ik929086/Documents/iDeer/output/Testing/simplified_polys_TEST.shp",, delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r Chunk-nfi_lcm_polys-into 5}
  }
  
  st_write(data, shp_path, delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
}, nfi_lcm_polys_2023_simplified, nfi_lcm_polys_2023_files))

#Read in shapefiles
my_shp_files <- list.files(simplified_nfi_lcm_polys_2023_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE)

my_shp_data <- lapply(my_shp_files, st_read)

#Calculate Area columns properly!! Then remove polygons < 0.01 ha
#At the moment there are millions of anomalous polygons that are really tiny
#This will massivly reduce the size of the dataset

# Process each shapefile: calculate area in hectares and filter polygons
my_shp_data_filtered <- lapply(my_shp_data, function(x) {
  # Ensure CRS is projected (not geographic) for accurate area calc
  if (st_is_longlat(x)) {
    stop("Input data is in geographic coordinates. Please reproject to a projected CRS before calculating area.")
  }

  x <- x %>%
    mutate(Area_Ha = as.numeric(st_area(.)) / 10000) %>%  # convert m² to ha
    filter(Area_Ha >= 0.01)
})

# Create new filenames with "_filtered.shp" suffix
filtered_shp_files <- sub("\\.shp$", "_filtered.shp", my_shp_files)

# Write filtered shapefiles
invisible(mapply(function(data, path) {
  st_write(data, path, delete_layer = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
}, my_shp_data_filtered, filtered_shp_files))

```
